title: The Off-Season Cliff: Why a Sporting Club's Best Month on the Field Is Its Riskiest Month in the Bank
linkedin:
Finals month is the best month of the year for a lot of suburban sporting clubs and academies. Gate takings, canteen and bar trade, sponsorship exposure, all peaking right now.

Here's the pattern we see once the season winds down. That healthy bank balance gets read as proof the club is in good shape, when it is actually the buffer the club needs to survive on for the next six months.

Revenue for most clubs and academies arrives in two short bursts, membership fees around sign-on and trading income around finals. Costs, ground hire, insurance, coaching wages, run close to flat all year. For junior academies, several of the biggest pre-season costs actually restart before a single dollar of next season's registration fees has been collected.

Clubs that get through the off-season comfortably are not the ones with the biggest finals month surplus. They are the ones who have mapped the full season cycle, trading peaks, sponsorship and grant timing, pre-season cost restarts, into one annual view instead of watching the balance month to month and hoping it holds.

A strong finals month is not bad news. It is the platform the rest of the year gets funded from. The question is whether it has been sized as a six month bridge or spent like it is the finish line.

A note for committees and owners running sporting clubs and junior sport academies across Brisbane, Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria: if finals month has left your club with its healthiest bank balance of the year, it is worth pausing before that surplus gets absorbed into presentation nights and season wind up costs.

The pattern we see is that most clubs and academies collect membership and registration fees in one burst near sign-on, then trading income peaks again around finals, while costs like ground hire, insurance and coaching wages stay fairly constant across the calendar. For junior academies, pre-season programs and coach retainers often begin before next season's fees are even collected.

The clubs that manage the off-season comfortably are the ones that have mapped that full cycle out in advance, rather than assuming this month's balance will simply carry them through. If your committee has not done that exercise yet, now, while the surplus is still sitting there, is the right time.
